description: This case study is the executive summary of the official report of the Fukushima Nuclear Accident Independent Investigation Commission, an inquiry established by the National Diet of Japan and published in July 2012 (88-page English PDF). It sets out the commission's mandate, a description of the 11 March 2011 accident including the plant cross-section with the 14-meter inundation level, conclusions and recommendations, and six findings chapters on whether the accident was preventable, escalation, emergency response, spread of the damage, organisational issues and the legal system. Appendices hold a survey of evacuees, a survey of workers, commission meeting reports and a glossary. Access: free PDF hosted by the Nuclear Information and Resource Service; the report is copyright the National Diet of Japan, all rights reserved. Coverage is the Fukushima Daiichi accident and Japanese nuclear governance. Caveats: the headline conclusion comes from search summaries, this hosted copy is not the original naiic.go.jp file, and only the front matter and overview pages were read. It suits cascading failure and emergency response studies of nuclear stations and their evacuation planning, and no directly related records are catalogued yet.

outcomes: The summary chapters ask whether the accident was preventable, how it escalated, how emergency response and damage spreading unfolded, and what organisational and legal-system issues lay behind it. The commission describes the loss of electricity, with the inundation level of 14 meters at the plant, making cooling and monitoring of the reactors very difficult, and includes surveys of evacuees and of workers. Search summaries give its headline conclusion that the accident was a profoundly manmade disaster that could and should have been foreseen and prevented.
